title: Effect of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs in the management of postoperative pain after cardiac surgery: A multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
official: Effect of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs in the management of postoperative pain after cardiac surgery: A multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
summary: Main objective: Show that the use of NSAIDs reduces pain 24 hours after cardiac surgery
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patient aged 18 or older admitted for elective cardiac surgery under extracorporeal circulation
2. Signed informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Thoracotomy approach, 2 Minimally invasive approach
2. Renal replacement therapy within the last 90 days
3. Depression with long-term treatment
4. History of gastrointestinal ulcer
5. Chronic use of NSAIDs before the operation
6. Opioid dependence or chronic opioid medication
7. Contraindications to the use of NSAIDs
8. Emergency surgery
9. Acute infectious endocarditis
10. AIDS with a CD4 count <200/mm3
11. Autoimmune disorder
12. Advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD 4 or 5)
